install.documented: uv venv unsloth_env --python 3.13; uv pip install unsloth --torch-backend=auto
install.ours: uv project depending on unsloth==2026.11.10 and parity (editable, so the reference runs in this environment); every transitive version constrained to the 2026-11-23 WSL spike's resolution of `uv pip install unsloth==2026.11.10` (docs/evidence/2026-11-23-m1-wsl-spike/freeze/unsloth.txt); pytest added for the adapter tests

deviations: CPU fallback instead of a GPU: Unsloth's fine-tuning docs assume an NVIDIA GPU (the Qwen3 page: 'fits comfortably in a Google Colab 16GB VRAM Tesla T4 GPU'). With no accelerator Unsloth 2026.11.10 takes its CPU route (unsloth/_cpu_init.py: 'stock transformers + PEFT + TRL'), and FastLanguageModel is unsloth_zoo.cpu.FastCPUModel, not the GPU loader. Verdicts describe Unsloth's CPU route.

GPU-only loader steps not exercised: the GPU loader's tokenizer repairs (unsloth/tokenizer_utils.py) and patched trainer don't run on CPU. Checked: the GPU path's post-load chat-template repair (_fix_chat_template_for_tokenizer) leaves Qwen3-0.6B's template unchanged, and Qwen3's pad token (<|endoftext|>) differs from its EOS, so the GPU pad-token repair would also leave it alone. Whether the GPU route's SFTTrainer patch changes TRL's EOS append or max_length is not verified.

load_in_4bit=True (the notebook's value) loads 16-bit weights on CPU: Unsloth's CPU loader decides this itself and says so ('loading 16-bit weights instead'). Weights are random and tiny; not on the data path.
Python 3.12, not the documented 3.13: Parity's core requires 3.12, and the spike resolved Unsloth on 3.12.
No --torch-backend=auto: the spike's plain install resolved torch 2.14.1 from PyPI's default Linux wheel.
runtime_settings: UNSLOTH_DISABLE_STATISTICS=1, set by the adapter before importing Unsloth (Unsloth's documented opt-out of its usage statistics download; on CPU the statistics call is not reached anyway).

The model is a tiny from_config Qwen3 (1 layer) saved to a local folder next to the real Qwen3-0.6B tokenizer, template and config files; loaded through FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained, so the loader's own tokenizer handling applies. No weights are downloaded.
